posts.title: Why Evals Are the New PRD: Specifying Non-Deterministic Products
posts.excerpt: Traditional PRDs assume deterministic if-then logic. When building with LLMs, your evaluation dataset is your true product specification. Here is a practical framework for writing Eval-Driven PRDs.

heroVisual.caption: From deterministic acceptance criteria to continuous evaluation loops.

body: For the last fifteen years, Product Managers wrote specifications around deterministic states: Given state A, when the user clicks B, the system returns C. With foundation models and agentic workflows, that contract breaks.
### The Shift from Rules to Distributions

An AI feature doesn't pass or fail a single binary test—it performs across a probability distribution of user intents, edge cases, and latency constraints. If you only write prose user stories, engineering and product end up debating anecdotal prompt outputs instead of shipping systematically.
### The 4-Part AI Product Spec
1. **Golden Dataset (25–50 real scenarios):** Before writing code, curate examples of ideal inputs, messy real-world inputs, and adversarial inputs alongside the expected rubric.
2. **Scoring Rubric (Code + LLM-as-Judge):** Define hard constraints (JSON schema validity, latency < 1.5s, zero PII leakage) and qualitative dimensions (tone, groundedness, actionability).
3. **Fallback & UX Guardrails:** What happens when confidence is low? Design graceful degradation before launch.
4. **Unit Economics Ceiling:** Token cost per successful task completion—not per API call.

posts.title: Prompting vs. RAG vs. Fine-Tuning: A Product Manager's Architecture Playbook
posts.excerpt: How to avoid the #1 costly mistake in AI product development: fine-tuning a model when you actually needed Retrieval-Augmented Generation (or a better prompt + eval loop).
body: One of the highest-leverage decisions an AI Product Manager makes with engineering is choosing the right adaptation pattern: In-Context Prompting, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), or Fine-Tuning.
### The Golden Rule: RAG is for Facts, Fine-Tuning is for Form
• Use Prompt Engineering + Context Caching first to establish your baseline quality and build your evaluation dataset.
• Use RAG when your product relies on dynamic, proprietary, or permission-scoped facts that change frequently and require verifiable source citations.

• Use Fine-Tuning (or distillation into a smaller model) when you need to teach a model a specialized output format, consistent brand voice, domain-specific syntax, or when you need to slash latency (<500ms) and per-token inference cost at scale.

posts.title: From Static PRDs to Live Code: The AI-Native PM Prototyping Stack
posts.excerpt: How product managers are using coding agents, Cursor/Antigravity, and synthetic data to validate product ideas with working software in 45 minutes instead of waiting two sprints.

heroVisual.caption: Full workflow walkthrough: Turning customer interview notes into an interactive web prototype.

body: The bottleneck in product discovery used to be translating a 6-page document into something a customer could actually react to. Today, an AI-fluent PM can go from raw customer call transcripts to an interactive coded prototype in a single afternoon.
### What We Cover in This Video Walkthrough
- **Step 1: Synthesizing Unstructured Discovery:** Extracting friction points across 20 user interviews without losing nuance.
- **Step 2: Rapid Interactive Prototyping:** Pairing with an AI coding agent to build a realistic front-end flow with real state.
- **Step 3: Live Customer Testing:** Why users give 10x more honest feedback when clicking a working prototype vs. viewing static slides.

posts.title: Case Study: Why Inline Diffs Beat Chat Sidebars in B2B Workflows
posts.excerpt: A visual teardown of 12 enterprise AI products showing why the 'slap a chatbot on the right side' era is ending—and the ambient UX patterns replacing it.

heroVisual.caption: Comparing prompt-heavy chat sidebars vs. context-aware inline actions across 12 products.

body: When generative AI first entered SaaS products, nearly every team shipped the exact same interface: a collapsible right-hand chat drawer that forced users to become prompt engineers.
### Key Findings from Our 12-Product Teardown
- **Blank-Canvas Paralysis:** 68% of enterprise users abandon open-ended chat boxes after their second session because typing context takes longer than doing the task manually.

- **The Winner—Ambient Next-Action Previews:** High-retention AI products pre-compute the likely action in the background and present a one-click `Tab-to-Accept` or inline diff directly inside the user's canvas.
- **Trust Through Provenance:** Showing *why* the model suggested an action (linking to the source ticket, doc, or metric) increased acceptance rates by 2.4x.

posts.title: Guest Interview: What Hiring Managers Actually Look for in AI Product Managers
posts.excerpt: We sat down with VP of Product leaders to unpack the difference between 'AI theater' on a resume and genuine AI product sense—plus how aspiring PMs can build proof-of-work.

heroVisual.caption: Episode #01 — Building proof of work in public vs. collecting certifications.

body: In our inaugural guest interview, we explore the #1 question aspiring and transitioning Product Managers ask: *How do I prove I can build AI products if my current company moves slowly?*
### Highlights from the Conversation
**Q: What separates a top 5% AI PM candidate right now?**

"They don't just talk about models; they show me something they built or evaluated over a weekend. When a candidate shares a GitHub repo or a live tool they shipped—and can explain where the model failed and how they fixed the prompt or UX—that immediately puts them at the top of the stack."
**Q: Do PMs need to be machine learning engineers?**
"No. You don't need to write custom CUDA kernels. You *do* need intuition for context windows, retrieval vs. fine-tuning trade-offs, latency budgets, and how to design an evaluation harness."
